Scripts for checking user/group membership and local permissions on remote servers.
Script Description Test-LocalAdminMembership.ps1 Check if a user/group is in the local Administrators group on remote servers

net localgroup Administrators for group membership query (broadly compatible, no ADSI required) Invoke-Command -Authentication Negotiate for domain auth Compact hostname Yes/No output format — easy to parse downstream
Checks whether a specified user or group is a local Administrator on remote servers.

Connects to each server via WinRM using provided credentials and checks membership in the local Administrators group using net localgroup Administrators. Outputs a compact <hostname> Yes/No line per server for easy downstream parsing.
Array of server hostnames or IPs to check.
The username or group name to check membership for.

Test-LocalAdminMembership.ps1 powershell <# .SYNOPSIS Checks whether a specified user or group is a local Administrator on remote servers. .DESCRIPTION Connects to each server via WinRM using provided credentials and checks membership in the local Administrators group using `net localgroup Administrators`. Outputs a compact "<hostname> Yes/No" line per server for easy downstream parsing. .PARAMETER User Username for WinRM authentication. .PARAMETER UserPassword Plaintext password (converted to SecureString internally). .PARAMETER Servers Array of server hostnames or IPs to check. .PARAMETER CheckMember The username or group name to check membership for. .EXAMPLE .\Test-LocalAdminMembership.ps1 -User "domain\admin" -UserPassword "pass" -Servers "srv01","srv02" -CheckMember "domain\svc-account" .TAGS admin, local-group, administrators, membership, check, remote, winrm, pscredential .NOTES Author: Jaineel Petiwale #> param ( [string]$User, [string]$UserPassword, [string[]]$Servers, [string]$CheckMember = "<user or group to check>" ) $secureStringPwd = ConvertTo-SecureString $UserPassword -AsPlainText -Force $credential = New-Object System.Management.Automation.PSCredential -ArgumentList $User, $secureStringPwd foreach ($server in $Servers) { try { Invoke-Command -ComputerName $server -Credential $credential -Authentication Negotiate -ErrorAction Stop -ScriptBlock { $hostname = $env:COMPUTERNAME $checkMember = $using:CheckMember $groupMembers = net localgroup Administrators if ($groupMembers -match [regex]::Escape($checkMember)) { Write-Host "$hostname Yes" } else { Write-Host "$hostname No" } } } catch { Write-Warning "Failed to connect to $server" } }
Scripts for copying files to remote Windows shares and SFTP servers.

Script Description Copy-FileToUNCPath.ps1 Simple Copy-Item to a UNC path (passthrough auth) Copy-FileWithCredentials.ps1 Map UNC as PSDrive with explicit credentials, copy, then clean up Invoke-SftpUpload.ps1 Upload a file via SFTP using WinSCP .NET assembly

New-PSDrive + Remove-PSDrive in finally for credentialed UNC access $cred PSCredential passed from caller scope (ServiceNow Orchestration compatible) WinSCP .NET assembly (WinSCPnet.dll) for SFTP — requires WinSCP installed SSH host key fingerprint stored in a .txt file — fetch once, reuse forever TransferMode = Binary as default for all file transfers
Run Invoke-SftpUpload.ps1 after: Installing WinSCP from https://winscp.net/eng/download.php Running the fingerprint fetch (see comments inside the script) to generate C:\Temp\sftp_fingerprint.txt
Copies a file to a UNC network share path using passthrough authentication.

Simple Copy-Item wrapper for UNC destinations. Uses the current session's passthrough credentials — no explicit credential mapping needed. Use Copy-FileWithCredentials.ps1 if explicit credentials are required.
Full local or network path of the source file.
Full UNC destination path including filename.

Copy-FileToUNCPath.ps1 powershell <# .SYNOPSIS Copies a file to a UNC network share path using passthrough authentication. .DESCRIPTION Simple Copy-Item wrapper for UNC destinations. Uses the current session's passthrough credentials — no explicit credential mapping needed. Use Copy-FileWithCredentials.ps1 if explicit credentials are required. .PARAMETER SourcePath Full local or network path of the source file. .PARAMETER DestinationPath Full UNC destination path including filename. .EXAMPLE .\Copy-FileToUNCPath.ps1 -SourcePath "D:\files\data.csv" -DestinationPath "\\server\share\data.csv" .TAGS copy, unc, file-transfer, network-share, passthrough-auth .NOTES Author: Jaineel Petiwale #> param ( [string]$SourcePath = "D:\OneStream_RITMs\production\Onestream_RITM10255120.csv", [string]$DestinationPath = "\\sacnt2192.americas.ad.flextronics.com\OneStream_PRD_NativeAndWeb\Onestream.csv" ) try { Copy-Item -Path $SourcePath -Destination $DestinationPath -ErrorAction Stop Write-Host "File copied successfully." } catch { Write-Host "Failed to copy file. Error: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
Maps a UNC path as a temporary PSDrive using explicit credentials and copies a file.

Creates a temporary mapped drive (Z:) using the provided $cred PSCredential, copies the source file to the mapped destination, then removes the drive in a finally block to ensure cleanup even on failure. $cred must be set in the caller scope (e.g., ServiceNow Orchestration or Get-Credential).
Full path of the source file to copy.
UNC path of the network share to map (without trailing backslash).
Filename to use at the destination.
Drive letter to use for the temporary mapping. Defaults to "Z:".

Copy-FileWithCredentials.ps1 powershell <# .SYNOPSIS Maps a UNC path as a temporary PSDrive using explicit credentials and copies a file. .DESCRIPTION Creates a temporary mapped drive (Z:) using the provided $cred PSCredential, copies the source file to the mapped destination, then removes the drive in a finally block to ensure cleanup even on failure. $cred must be set in the caller scope (e.g., ServiceNow Orchestration or Get-Credential). .PARAMETER SourcePath Full path of the source file to copy. .PARAMETER DestinationUNC UNC path of the network share to map (without trailing backslash). .PARAMETER DestinationFile Filename to use at the destination. .PARAMETER DriveLetter Drive letter to use for the temporary mapping. Defaults to "Z:". .EXAMPLE $cred = Get-Credential .\Copy-FileWithCredentials.ps1 -SourcePath "D:\data.csv" -DestinationUNC "\\server\share" -DestinationFile "output.csv" .TAGS copy, unc, file-transfer, psdrive, pscredential, network-share, map-drive .NOTES Author: Jaineel Petiwale #> param ( [string]$SourcePath = "D:\OneStream_RITMs\production\Onestream_RITM10255120.csv", [string]$DestinationUNC = "\\sacnt2192.americas.ad.flextronics.com\OneStream_PRD_NativeAndWeb", [string]$DestinationFile = "Onestream.csv", [string]$DriveLetter = "Z:" ) $driveName = $DriveLetter.TrimEnd(':') try { New-PSDrive -Name $driveName -PSProvider FileSystem -Root $DestinationUNC -Credential $cred -ErrorAction Stop Copy-Item -Path $SourcePath -Destination "$DriveLetter\$DestinationFile" -ErrorAction Stop Write-Host "File copied successfully." } catch { Write-Host "An error occurred: $($_.Exception.Message)" } finally { if (Get-PSDrive -Name $driveName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { Remove-PSDrive -Name $driveName -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } }
Uploads a file to an SFTP server using the WinSCP .NET assembly.

Loads WinSCPnet.dll, reads a stored SSH host key fingerprint from a file, opens an SFTP session, and uploads a local file to the remote path. The fingerprint file must be generated once using the companion fetch block included in the NOTES section below. Prerequisite: WinSCP installed at C:\Program Files (x86)\WinSCP\ One-time: Run the fingerprint fetch block below to populate $FingerprintPath.
Full local path of the file to upload.
Path to the stored SSH host key fingerprint file.
Path to WinSCPnet.dll. Defaults to standard install location.

Author: Jaineel Petiwale --- ONE-TIME FINGERPRINT FETCH --- Run this block once to save the fingerprint, then use Invoke-SftpUpload.ps1 normally: powershell $logPath = "C:\Temp\winscp_log.txt" $fingerprintPath = "C:\Temp\sftp_fingerprint.txt" $host = "sftp.example.com" $username = "your_username" $password = "your_password" $cmd = "/log=""$logPath"" /command ""open sftp://$username:`"$password`"@$host/"" ""exit""" Start-Process -FilePath "C:\Program Files (x86)\WinSCP\WinSCP.exe" -ArgumentList $cmd -NoNewWindow -Wait Start-Sleep -Seconds 3 $fingerprint = Select-String -Path $logPath -Pattern "Host key fingerprint is .*" | ForEach-Object { ($_ -split "is")[1].Trim() } if ($fingerprint) { $fingerprint | Out-File $fingerprintPath -Encoding utf8 Write-Host "Fingerprint saved to $fingerprintPath" } else { Write-Error "Failed to extract fingerprint" } --- END FETCH BLOCK ---

Invoke-SftpUpload.ps1 powershell <# .SYNOPSIS Uploads a file to an SFTP server using the WinSCP .NET assembly. .DESCRIPTION Loads WinSCPnet.dll, reads a stored SSH host key fingerprint from a file, opens an SFTP session, and uploads a local file to the remote path. The fingerprint file must be generated once using the companion fetch block included in the NOTES section below. Prerequisite: WinSCP installed at C:\Program Files (x86)\WinSCP\ One-time: Run the fingerprint fetch block below to populate $FingerprintPath. .PARAMETER LocalPath Full local path of the file to upload. .PARAMETER RemotePath Remote SFTP directory path (e.g., "/upload/"). .PARAMETER HostName SFTP server hostname or IP. .PARAMETER UserName SFTP username. .PARAMETER Password SFTP password. .PARAMETER FingerprintPath Path to the stored SSH host key fingerprint file. .PARAMETER WinScpDllPath Path to WinSCPnet.dll. Defaults to standard install location. .EXAMPLE .\Invoke-SftpUpload.ps1 -LocalPath "C:\data\file.csv" -RemotePath "/upload/" -HostName "sftp.example.com" -UserName "user" -Password "pass" .TAGS sftp, winscp, winscpnet, upload, fingerprint, secure, binary .NOTES Author: Jaineel Petiwale --- ONE-TIME FINGERPRINT FETCH --- Run this block once to save the fingerprint, then use Invoke-SftpUpload.ps1 normally: $logPath = "C:\Temp\winscp_log.txt" $fingerprintPath = "C:\Temp\sftp_fingerprint.txt" $host = "sftp.example.com" $username = "your_username" $password = "your_password" $cmd = "/log=""$logPath"" /command ""open sftp://$username:`"$password`"@$host/"" ""exit""" Start-Process -FilePath "C:\Program Files (x86)\WinSCP\WinSCP.exe" -ArgumentList $cmd -NoNewWindow -Wait Start-Sleep -Seconds 3 $fingerprint = Select-String -Path $logPath -Pattern "Host key fingerprint is .*" | ForEach-Object { ($_ -split "is")[1].Trim() } if ($fingerprint) { $fingerprint | Out-File $fingerprintPath -Encoding utf8 Write-Host "Fingerprint saved to $fingerprintPath" } else { Write-Error "Failed to extract fingerprint" } --- END FETCH BLOCK --- #> param ( [string]$LocalPath = "C:\Local\Path\file.txt", [string]$RemotePath = "/remote/path/", [string]$HostName = "sftp.example.com", [string]$UserName = "your_username", [string]$Password = "your_password", [string]$FingerprintPath = "C:\Temp\sftp_fingerprint.txt", [string]$WinScpDllPath = "C:\Program Files (x86)\WinSCP\WinSCPnet.dll" ) Add-Type -Path $WinScpDllPath if (-not (Test-Path $FingerprintPath)) { Write-Error "Fingerprint file not found at '$FingerprintPath'. Run the one-time fetch block in NOTES first." exit 1 } $fingerprint = Get-Content $FingerprintPath -Raw $sessionOptions = New-Object WinSCP.SessionOptions -Property @{ Protocol = [WinSCP.Protocol]::Sftp HostName = $HostName UserName = $UserName Password = $Password PortNumber = 22 SshHostKeyFingerprint = $fingerprint } $session = New-Object WinSCP.Session try { $session.Open($sessionOptions) $transferOptions = New-Object WinSCP.TransferOptions $transferOptions.TransferMode = [WinSCP.TransferMode]::Binary $result = $session.PutFiles($LocalPath, $RemotePath, $False, $transferOptions) $result.Check() foreach ($transfer in $result.Transfers) { Write-Host "✅ Upload succeeded: $($transfer.FileName)" } } catch { Write-Error "❌ Upload failed: $($_.Exception.Message)" } finally { $session.Dispose() }
Scripts for WinRM-based remote command execution and Windows service management.

Script Description Invoke-RemoteCommand.ps1 Execute a script block on a remote host via WinRM Get-ServicesByKeyword.ps1 Query services on multiple remote servers by keyword Set-ServiceState.ps1 Stop/start services matching keywords across multiple servers

PSCredential construction: ConvertTo-SecureString + New-Object System.Management.Automation.PSCredential WinRM pre-check: Test-WSMan before Invoke-Command FQDN resolution: Resolve-DnsName with IP fallback -Authentication Negotiate for domain environments [SNCLOG] log prefix for ServiceNow Orchestration output parsing $using:variable to pass outer-scope variables into remote script blocks Get-WmiObject Win32_Service for service enumeration (pre-PS7 compatible)
Resolves a list of domain names to their IP addresses.

Accepts an array of domain names and resolves each to its first available IP address using the .NET DNS resolver. Outputs a domain -> IP mapping. Unresolvable domains are marked as "Could not resolve".
Array of domain names to resolve.

Get-IpFromDomainList.ps1 powershell <# .SYNOPSIS Resolves a list of domain names to their IP addresses. .DESCRIPTION Accepts an array of domain names and resolves each to its first available IP address using the .NET DNS resolver. Outputs a domain -> IP mapping. Unresolvable domains are marked as "Could not resolve". .PARAMETER DomainNames Array of domain names to resolve. .EXAMPLE .\Get-IpFromDomainList.ps1 -DomainNames "google.com", "github.com", "nonexistent.local" .TAGS dns, ip, resolve, domain, bulk, network .NOTES Author: Jaineel Petiwale #> param ( [string[]]$DomainNames ) $ipAddresses = @{} foreach ($domain in $DomainNames) { try { $ip = [System.Net.Dns]::GetHostAddresses($domain) | Select-Object -First 1 $ipAddresses[$domain] = $ip.IPAddressToString } catch { $ipAddresses[$domain] = "Could not resolve" } } foreach ($domain in $ipAddresses.Keys) { Write-Output "$domain -> $($ipAddresses[$domain])" }
Connects to a remote Windows host via WinRM and executes a script block.

Validates WinRM availability on the target, resolves the hostname to FQDN, and executes a command remotely using provided PSCredential. Designed for use in ServiceNow Orchestration — all log lines are prefixed with [SNCLOG] for Orchestration output parsing. The $command script block and $cred PSCredential are expected to be set in the caller scope (e.g., ServiceNow Orchestration activity variables).
Hostname or IP of the target machine.

Invoke-RemoteCommand.ps1 powershell <# .SYNOPSIS Connects to a remote Windows host via WinRM and executes a script block. .DESCRIPTION Validates WinRM availability on the target, resolves the hostname to FQDN, and executes a command remotely using provided PSCredential. Designed for use in ServiceNow Orchestration — all log lines are prefixed with [SNCLOG] for Orchestration output parsing. The $command script block and $cred PSCredential are expected to be set in the caller scope (e.g., ServiceNow Orchestration activity variables). .PARAMETER Computer Hostname or IP of the target machine. .PARAMETER Cred PSCredential object for authentication. .EXAMPLE $cred = Get-Credential $computer = "server01.example.com" .\Invoke-RemoteCommand.ps1 .TAGS winrm, invoke-command, remote, pscredential, wsman, servicenow, orchestration, logging .NOTES Author: Jaineel Petiwale #> # Start transcript logging $timestamp = (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString("yyyy-MM-ddTHH-mm-ss\Z") $logFile = "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\script_log_$timestamp.log" Start-Transcript -Path $logFile -Append # Command to execute on the remote system $command = { "Remote Hostname: $env:COMPUTERNAME" "Remote Current User: $env:USERNAME" } ### Do not modify below unless intentional ### if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($computer)) { Write-Error "[SNCLOG] Computer name/IP not provided." return } if (-not ($cred -is [System.Management.Automation.PSCredential])) { Write-Error "[SNCLOG] Invalid or missing credentials." return } # Resolve to FQDN if IP provided; trim trailing dot if present $resolvedComputer = (Resolve-DnsName -Name $computer -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).NameHost if (-not $resolvedComputer) { $resolvedComputer = $computer } # Pre-check WinRM availability if (-not (Test-WSMan -ComputerName $resolvedComputer -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Write-Error "[SNCLOG] $resolvedComputer is reachable but WinRM is not available." return } Write-Output "[SNCLOG] Connecting to $resolvedComputer and executing command..." try { Invoke-Command -ComputerName $resolvedComputer -Credential $cred -ScriptBlock $command -ErrorAction Stop } catch { Write-Error "[SNCLOG] Error: $($_.Exception.Message)" } Write-Output "[SNCLOG] Command execution completed." Stop-Transcript
Retrieves Windows services matching a keyword from multiple remote servers.

Connects to each server in the provided list via WinRM and queries Win32_Service for services whose Name, DisplayName, or Description matches the given keyword. Outputs a formatted table per server including: Name, Display Name, Logon As, State, and Description. Continues to the next server on failure.
Plaintext password for authentication (converted to SecureString internally).
Array of server hostnames or IPs to connect to.
Keyword string to filter services by. Defaults to "MID".

Get-ServicesByKeyword.ps1 powershell <# .SYNOPSIS Retrieves Windows services matching a keyword from multiple remote servers. .DESCRIPTION Connects to each server in the provided list via WinRM and queries Win32_Service for services whose Name, DisplayName, or Description matches the given keyword. Outputs a formatted table per server including: Name, Display Name, Logon As, State, and Description. Continues to the next server on failure. .PARAMETER User Username for WinRM authentication. .PARAMETER UserPassword Plaintext password for authentication (converted to SecureString internally). .PARAMETER Servers Array of server hostnames or IPs to connect to. .PARAMETER Keyword Keyword string to filter services by. Defaults to "MID". .EXAMPLE .\Get-ServicesByKeyword.ps1 -User "domain\admin" -UserPassword "pass" -Servers "srv01","srv02" -Keyword "MID" .TAGS service, wmi, win32_service, keyword, filter, remote, winrm, table, report .NOTES Author: Jaineel Petiwale #> param ( [string]$User, [string]$UserPassword, [string[]]$Servers, [string]$Keyword = "MID" ) $secureStringPwd = ConvertTo-SecureString $UserPassword -AsPlainText -Force $credential = New-Object System.Management.Automation.PSCredential -ArgumentList $User, $secureStringPwd Write-Host "`n# $Keyword Windows Services Search Report — $(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss') $((Get-TimeZone).Id)`n---" -ForegroundColor Green foreach ($server in $Servers) { Write-Host "## $server`n" -ForegroundColor Yellow try { Invoke-Command -ComputerName $server -Credential $credential -Authentication Negotiate -ErrorAction Stop -ScriptBlock { $hostname = $env:COMPUTERNAME $keyword = $using:Keyword $services = Get-WmiObject Win32_Service | Where-Object { $_.Name -match $keyword -or $_.DisplayName -match $keyword -or $_.Description -match $keyword } | Sort-Object State | ForEach-Object { [PSCustomObject]@{ Name = $_.Name DisplayName = $_.DisplayName LogonAs = $_.StartName State = $_.State Description = $_.Description } } $maxName = [Math]::Max(($services.Name | Measure-Object -Property Length -Maximum).Maximum, 25) $maxDisplayName = [Math]::Max(($services.DisplayName | Measure-Object -Property Length -Maximum).Maximum, 30) $maxLogonAs = [Math]::Max(($services.LogonAs | Measure-Object -Property Length -Maximum).Maximum, 30) $maxState = [Math]::Max(($services.State | Measure-Object -Property Length -Maximum).Maximum, 10) $maxDescription = [Math]::Max(($services.Description | Measure-Object -Property Length -Maximum).Maximum, 40) Write-Host "**Hostname**: ``$hostname```n" -ForegroundColor Cyan if ($services.Count -eq 0) { Write-Host "No '$keyword' services found on $hostname." -ForegroundColor DarkYellow return } Write-Host ("{0,-$maxName} | {1,-$maxDisplayName} | {2,-$maxLogonAs} | {3,-$maxState} | {4,-$maxDescription}" ` -f "Name", "Display Name", "Logon As", "State", "Description") Write-Host ("{0,-$maxName} | {1,-$maxDisplayName} | {2,-$maxLogonAs} | {3,-$maxState} | {4,-$maxDescription}" ` -f ("-" * $maxName), ("-" * $maxDisplayName), ("-" * $maxLogonAs), ("-" * $maxState), ("-" * $maxDescription)) foreach ($svc in $services) { Write-Host ("{0,-$maxName} | {1,-$maxDisplayName} | {2,-$maxLogonAs} | {3,-$maxState} | {4,-$maxDescription}" ` -f $svc.Name, $svc.DisplayName, $svc.LogonAs, $svc.State, $svc.Description) } } } catch { Write-Warning "Failed to connect to $server : $_" } Write-Host "`n---" }
Stops running services matching all provided keywords across multiple remote servers.

Connects to each server via WinRM and stops any Running service whose name matches ALL keywords in the Keywords array (AND logic). Outputs success/failure per service. Extend the script block to support Start-Service for a start action variant.
Array of server hostnames or IPs.
Array of keyword strings — service name must match ALL of them. Defaults to "MID","ServiceNow".

Set-ServiceState.ps1 powershell <# .SYNOPSIS Stops running services matching all provided keywords across multiple remote servers. .DESCRIPTION Connects to each server via WinRM and stops any Running service whose name matches ALL keywords in the Keywords array (AND logic). Outputs success/failure per service. Extend the script block to support Start-Service for a start action variant. .PARAMETER User Username for WinRM authentication. .PARAMETER UserPassword Plaintext password (converted to SecureString internally). .PARAMETER Servers Array of server hostnames or IPs. .PARAMETER Keywords Array of keyword strings — service name must match ALL of them. Defaults to "MID","ServiceNow". .EXAMPLE .\Set-ServiceState.ps1 -User "domain\admin" -UserPassword "pass" -Servers "srv01","srv02" -Keywords "MID","ServiceNow" .TAGS service, stop, start, keyword, remote, winrm, pscredential, bulk .NOTES Author: Jaineel Petiwale #> param ( [string]$User, [string]$UserPassword, [string[]]$Servers, [string[]]$Keywords = @("MID", "ServiceNow") ) $secureStringPwd = ConvertTo-SecureString $UserPassword -AsPlainText -Force $credential = New-Object System.Management.Automation.PSCredential -ArgumentList $User, $secureStringPwd foreach ($server in $Servers) { try { Invoke-Command -ComputerName $server -Credential $credential -Authentication Negotiate -ScriptBlock { param($keywords) function MatchesAllKeywords { param($serviceName, $keywords) foreach ($word in $keywords) { if ($serviceName -notlike "*$word*") { return $false } } return $true } foreach ($svc in (Get-Service)) { if ($svc.Status -eq 'Running' -and (MatchesAllKeywords -serviceName $svc.Name -keywords $keywords)) { try { Stop-Service -Name $svc.Name -Force Write-Output "[$env:COMPUTERNAME] ✅ Stopped: $($svc.Name)" } catch { Write-Output "[$env:COMPUTERNAME] ❌ Failed to stop: $($svc.Name) — $_" } } } } -ArgumentList $Keywords -ErrorAction Stop } catch { Write-Output "❗ Error connecting to ${server}: $_" } }

ServiceNow administrators frequently need to manage scheduled jobs, execute them in bulk, or troubleshoot jobs that are stuck. This guide explains how to programmatically handle these scenarios using Background Scripts.

When dealing with multiple scheduled data imports, reports, or other scheduled items, it is tedious to trigger them manually. You can use the SncTriggerSynchronizer API to execute jobs programmatically. APIs Used: SncTriggerSynchronizer.executeNow(GlideRecord) - Forces a scheduled job to execute immediately. GlideRecord - For querying the target jobs (e.g., scheduled_import_set or sysauto_report). Example Script: javascript var table = 'scheduled_import_set'; // Or use 'sysauto_report' for reports var field = 'data_source'; // Or 'report_title' // Array of sys_ids for the data sources or scheduled jobs var range = [ '4096f49adba6b890c7cfc0a239961938', '3c373812dbe6b890c7cfc0a23996192f', 'bfba3ba2db3c60108150b177f49619b4' ]; var gr = new GlideRecord(table); // Dynamically build the encoded query for all sys_ids gr.addEncodedQuery(`${field}=${range.join(`^OR${field}=`)}`); gr.query(); while (gr.next()) { gs.info("Executing: " + gr.getDisplayValue()); // Trigger the job immediately SncTriggerSynchronizer.executeNow(gr); }

Sometimes scheduled jobs get "stuck" in a running or queued state, particularly if they are claimed by a node that no longer exists (e.g., after an instance clone or node restart). This script checks the sys_trigger table for jobs claimed by invalid nodes. APIs Used: GlideRecord('sys_trigger') - The core table storing all scheduled and triggered events. GlideRecord('sys_cluster_state') - Stores active node information. Example Script: javascript showScheduledJobsStuckOnMissingNodes(); function showScheduledJobsStuckOnMissingNodes() { var gr = new GlideRecord('sys_trigger'); // Query only jobs that are queued (1) or running (2) gr.addQuery('state', 'IN', '1,2'); // Filter out those that are not claimed by any node gr.addQuery('claimed_by', '!=', 'NULL'); // Check against valid nodes in the cluster var gr2 = new GlideRecord('sys_cluster_state'); gr2.query(); while (gr2.next()) { // Filter out any valid system_id values. What remains are invalid claims. gr.addQuery('claimed_by', '!=', gr2.system_id); } gr.query(); // Display a warning for each suspect scheduled job while (gr.next()) { gs.print('WARNING: sys_trigger.' + gr.sys_id + ' has a state of ' + gr.state + ' and is claimed by missing node: ' + gr.claimed_by); } }
This guide covers programmatic ways to manage users, update passwords, and handle active sessions across ServiceNow instances using both Background Scripts (GlideRecord) and NodeJS (OOTB REST APIs).

Sometimes you need to programmatically create a user and assign them specific roles (like admin and security_admin) along with custom user preferences. APIs Used: GlideRecord('sys_user') - For creating the user record. GlideSecurityManager.get().enableElevatedRole() - Required to assign security_admin. sys_user_has_role and sys_user_preference tables for relationships. javascript // Create the user record var grSysUser = new GlideRecord("sys_user"); grSysUser.initialize(); grSysUser.setNewGuidValue('jaineelpetiwale'); // Set custom sys_id (optional, usually auto-generated) grSysUser.setDisplayValue('user_name', 'jaineel.petiwale'); grSysUser.setDisplayValue('first_name', 'Jaineel'); grSysUser.setDisplayValue('last_name', 'Petiwale'); grSysUser.setDisplayValue('email', 'Jaineel2001@gmail.com'); grSysUser.setDisplayValue('title', 'ServiceNow Developer'); grSysUser.setDisplayValue('department', 'IT'); grSysUser.setValue('preferred_language','en'); grSysUser.setDisplayValue('gender','Male'); grSysUser.setDisplayValue('identity_type', 'human'); grSysUser.setDisplayValue('manager','admin'); grSysUser.setValue('active', true); grSysUser.setDisplayValue('user_password', 'MySecretPassword123'); // Set the password grSysUser.setValue('password_needs_reset', false); // System fields (sys_created_on/by) can be overridden if needed grSysUser.setValue('sys_created_on', '2001-03-21 05:30:00'); grSysUser.setValue('sys_created_by', 'jaineel.petiwale'); grSysUser.autoSysFields(); // Ensure sys fields are handled var userSysId = grSysUser.insert(); // Set the password using GlideSystem, assign roles, and set preferences if (userSysId) { // Assign admin and security_admin roles GlideSecurityManager.get().enableElevatedRole('security_admin'); addRole(userSysId, "admin"); addRole(userSysId, "security_admin"); GlideSecurityManager.get().disableElevatedRole('security_admin'); gs.info("Roles 'admin' and 'security_admin' assigned to the user."); // Set "Always Show Top Navigation" preference for UI16/Polaris setUserPreference(userSysId, "glide.ui.polaris.ui16_tabs_inside_polaris", true); gs.info("User preference 'Always Show Top Navigation' set to true."); } else { gs.info("User creation failed."); } // Function to assign a role to a user function addRole(userSysId, roleName) { var grSysUserHasRole = new GlideRecord("sys_user_has_role"); grSysUserHasRole.initialize(); grSysUserHasRole.setValue('user', userSysId); grSysUserHasRole.role.setDisplayValue(roleName); grSysUserHasRole.insert(); } // Function to set user preference function setUserPreference(userSysId, name, value) { var grSysUserPreference = new GlideRecord("sys_user_preference"); grSysUserPreference.initialize(); grSysUserPreference.setValue('user', userSysId); grSysUserPreference.setDisplayValue('name', name); grSysUserPreference.setValue('value', value); grSysUserPreference.insert(); }

documents.t: If you just need to reset a password for a specific user using their sys_id, you can simply update the user_password field via setDisplayValue. APIs Used: GlideRecord .get() and .update() javascript var grSysUser = new GlideRecord('sys_user'); if (grSysUser.get('PUT_USER_SYS_ID_HERE')) { grSysUser.user_password.setDisplayValue('new_password_here'); grSysUser.update(); }
documents.s: 2. Quickly Updating a Local User Password (Background Script)

documents.t: Using the NodeJS script below, you can generate a strong randomized password and update a non-admin user's password across multiple ServiceNow instances using the Table API. APIs Used: Table API (/api/now/table/sys_user/{sys_id}?sysparm_input_display_value=true) Native NodeJS https and crypto modules javascript import https from 'https'; import { randomBytes } from 'crypto'; import { URL } from 'url'; // List of ServiceNow instances (e.g., 'dev12345') const instances = ['dev225514']; // Service account credentials const username = 'your_username'; const password = 'your_password'; const userSysId = 'PUT_USER_SYS_ID_HERE'; // Generate a secure 20-character alphanumeric password function generatePassword(length = 20) { const charset = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789'; const bytes = randomBytes(length); return Array.from(bytes).map(b => charset[b % charset.length]).join(''); } // Make an HTTPS PATCH request to update the password via Table API function updatePassword(instanceUrl, userSysId, newPassword, username, password) { return new Promise((resolve, reject) => { // Note: sysparm_input_display_value=true is crucial when setting passwords directly const apiUrl = new URL(`/api/now/table/sys_user/${userSysId}?sysparm_input_display_value=true`, `https://${instanceUrl}.service-now.com`); const body = JSON.stringify({ user_password: newPassword }); const auth = Buffer.from(`${username}:${password}`).toString('base64'); const options = { method: 'PATCH', headers: { 'Authorization': `Basic ${auth}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Content-Length': Buffer.byteLength(body) } }; const req = https.request(apiUrl, options, res => { let data = ''; res.on('data', chunk => data += chunk); res.on('end', () => { if (res.statusCode >= 200 && res.statusCode < 300) { resolve(`Success: ${instanceUrl}`); } else { reject(`Failed on ${instanceUrl}: ${res.statusCode} - ${data}`); } }); }); req.on('error', reject); req.write(body); req.end(); }); } (async () => { const newPassword = generatePassword(); console.log(`Generated Password: ${newPassword}`); for (const instance of instances) { try { const result = await updatePassword(instance, userSysId, newPassword, username, password); console.log(result); } catch (err) { console.error(err); } } })();
documents.s: 3. Bulk Updating User Passwords across Instances (NodeJS)

documents.t: If a user is compromised or needs their session invalidated immediately across all nodes, use the GlideSessions API. APIs Used: GlideSessions.lockOutSessionsInAllNodes(username) javascript // Forcefully invalidates all active sessions for the specified user GlideSessions.lockOutSessionsInAllNodes("<username>");
This article covers miscellaneous system-level utilities in ServiceNow, including impersonating the "System" user, manipulating time formats, canceling records in bulk, and decrypting credentials.

Sometimes background tasks or bulk updates need to bypass user security rules or be logged as the "System". Furthermore, understanding how GlideDateTime formats time in UTC vs Local Server Time is crucial. APIs Used: gs.getSession().impersonate("system") - Bypasses standard user context. GlideDateTime - Handles time manipulation. javascript // Impersonate the System user var systemUser = gs.getSession().impersonate("system"); var gdt = new GlideDateTime(); // Always UTC +0 gs.print("UTC Time: " + gdt.getValue()); gs.print("Timezone Offset (ms): " + gdt.getTZOffset()); // Difference from UTC gs.print("Server Internal Format: " + gdt.getDisplayValueInternal()); // Local time in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss gs.print("Local Formatted Time: " + gdt.getDisplayValue()); // Local formatted time based on session // Revert back to the original user gs.getSession().impersonate(systemUser);
documents.s: 1. Impersonating the System User & Managing Time

documents.t: When performing mass updates (like canceling incidents after a monthly maintenance window), running it as the "System" ensures you don't trigger unnecessary notifications designed for human agents, and audit logs correctly attribute the change to the system. APIs Used: gs.getSession().impersonate() GlideRecord update operations. javascript var cancel_note = 'This failure alert is due to monthly maintenance activity. By default post maintenance, we have already rerun all the failed jobs, which went to success and hence we are canceling this incident. Cancelled from backend by SNC Team.'; var grIncident = new GlideRecord('incident'); grIncident.addEncodedQuery("number=INC16349771"); // Example target grIncident.setLimit(50); grIncident.query(); while (grIncident.next()) { // Impersonate system before the update var originalUser = gs.getSession().impersonate("system"); grIncident.incident_state = 8; // Cancelled grIncident.comment = cancel_note; grIncident.close_notes = cancel_note; grIncident.update(); // Immediately revert impersonation gs.getSession().impersonate(originalUser); }
documents.s: 2. Canceling Incidents in Bulk as System

documents.t: In advanced integration or troubleshooting scenarios, you might need to decrypt a password stored securely in a ServiceNow credentials record or an encrypted field. APIs Used: sn_cc.StandardCredentialsProvider() - Modern API for fetching credentials securely. GlideEncrypter() - Lower-level API for decrypting specific encrypted fields. Option 1: Using Standard Credentials Provider javascript // Fetch password from the Discovery/Orchestration Credentials table var provider = new sn_cc.StandardCredentialsProvider(); var credentials = provider.getCredentialByID("<credential sys_id>"); var password = credentials.getAttribute("password"); gs.info("Decrypted Password: " + password); Option 2: Using GlideEncrypter javascript // Decrypt a specific Two-Way Encrypted field (e.g., jdbc_password) var encrypter = new GlideEncrypter(); gs.log("Decrypted DB Password: " + encrypter.decrypt(grSDS.jdbc_password));

Managing Update Sets in ServiceNow often involves moving records that aren't natively captured or deploying update sets across environments automatically. This guide details how to perform these operations using both Background Scripts and NodeJS integrations via the CI/CD Spoke APIs.

Sometimes you need to retroactively add several records to a specific update set. The GlideUpdateManager2 API allows you to force a record into the current active update set. APIs Used: GlideUpdateManager2().saveRecord() - Adds a given GlideRecord to the current update set. [!WARNING] Before running this script, ensure you have selected the correct Update Set as your "Current" active update set in the ServiceNow UI. javascript // Example: Adding specific records (e.g., from an item_option_new table) to the update set var gr = new GlideRecord('sys_update_set'); // Modify the query below to target the records you wish to force into the update set gr.addEncodedQuery("nameSTARTSWITH<update_set_name>"); gr.query(); var um = new GlideUpdateManager2(); // Loop through the query results and add each record to the current update set while (gr.next()) { var recSysID = gr.getUniqueValue(); gs.info("Adding record to update set: " + recSysID); // Save to current update set um.saveRecord(gr); } gs.info("Added all records from table to the current update set");
documents.s: 1. Adding Multiple Existing Records to an Update Set (Background Script)

documents.t: Occasionally, when retrieving update sets from another instance, the process hangs or fails with the error: Update set retrieve is unavailable because another operation 'Committing update set: <Update_Set_name>' is running This happens when a mutex lock is not properly released. Fix: Navigate to sys_mutex.LIST in the filter navigator. Search for the record with the name update-mutex. Delete that record from the sys_mutex table to release the lock.
documents.s: 2. Resolving Update Set Retrieval Mutex Errors

documents.t:
Instead of manually retrieving, previewing, and committing Update Sets via the UI, you can fully automate the process using the sn_cicd REST APIs. The following NodeJS script takes an Update Set sys_id and orchestrates the deployment from an origin instance to a target instance. APIs Used: GET /api/now/table/sys_update_set - Validates the update set is marked "Complete" on the origin. GET /api/now/table/sys_update_set_source - Finds the update source record on the target instance. POST /api/sn_cicd/update_set/retrieve - Triggers retrieval and auto-preview. POST /api/sn_cicd/update_set/commit/{remote_update_set_id} - Commits the retrieved update set. [!NOTE] This requires the ServiceNow CI/CD Spoke plugin to be active on the target instance. javascript import { request as _request } from "https"; // ... (readline setup omitted for brevity - see full repository for interactive prompts) ... async function deployUpdateSet(updateSetId, originInstance, targetInstance, user, pass) { // Step 1: Validate update set is marked complete on origin console.log(`
[Step 1] Validating update set is complete on ${originInstance}...`); const valRes = await request(originInstance, "GET", `/api/now/table/sys_update_set?sysparm_query=sys_id=${updateSetId}&sysparm_fields=name,state&sysparm_limit=1` ); const usRecord = valRes.body?.result?.[0]; if (usRecord.state !== "complete") throw new Error(`Update set is not complete.`); // Step 2: Get update set source for origin on target console.log(`
[Step 2] Fetching update source for ${originInstance} from ${targetInstance}...`); const srcRes = await request(targetInstance, "GET", `/api/now/table/sys_update_set_source?sysparm_fields=sys_id,name,instance_id&sysparm_query=active=true^urlLIKE${originInstance}.service-now.com` ); const updateSourceId = srcRes.body?.result[0].sys_id; const updateSourceInstanceId = srcRes.body?.result[0].instance_id; // Step 3: Retrieve update set on target with auto_preview + cleanup console.log(`
[Step 3] Retrieving update set on ${targetInstance}...`); const retrieveRes = await request(targetInstance, "POST", `/api/sn_cicd/update_set/retrieve?update_set_id=${updateSetId}&update_source_id=${updateSourceId}&update_source_instance_id=${updateSourceInstanceId}&auto_preview=true&cleanup_retrieved=true` ); // The API is asynchronous; it returns a progress URL. const progressUrl = retrieveRes.body?.result?.links?.progress?.url; // Step 4: Poll retrieve/preview progress (Helper function repeatedly calls GET on progressUrl) console.log(`
[Step 4] Polling retrieve + preview progress...`); const progressResult = await pollProgress(targetInstance, progressUrl); // Extract the remote update set ID once preview completes const remoteUpdateSetId = progressResult.remote_update_set_id || progressResult.links?.result?.id; // Step 5: Commit remote update set console.log(`
[Step 5] Committing remote update set ${remoteUpdateSetId}...`); const commitRes = await requestWithBody(targetInstance, "POST", `/api/sn_cicd/update_set/commit/${remoteUpdateSetId}`, { force_commit: "true" } ); const commitProgressUrl = commitRes.body?.result?.links?.progress?.url; // Poll commit progress await pollProgress(targetInstance, commitProgressUrl); console.log("
✓ Update set deployed successfully."); }

This plugin loads a supplementary security model to the itil role that allows specific roles to be assigned for each application in the ITSM suite. ITSM Roles - Incident Management updates the Incident Management security model to factor two new roles: sn_incident_read and sn_incident_write ITSM Roles - Problem Management updates the Problem Management security model to factor two new roles: sn_problem_read and sn_problem_write ITSM Roles - Change Management updates the Change Management security model to factor two new roles: sn_change_read and sn_change_write ITSM Roles - Request Management updates the Request Management security model to factor two new roles: sn_request_read and sn_request_write IMPORTANT: This plugin loads new Access Controls for the applications listed above, read the release notes and documentation to understand the full impact of this plugin.

Table Description sys_ui_bookmark Table stores user-level bookmarks for specific pages or UI elements within the ServiceNow platform. This allows users to easily navigate to frequently accessed content. sys_ui_bookmark_group Table stores user-level bookmark Groupswithin the ServiceNow platform. This allows users to easily navigate to frequently accessed content. sys_user_presence Table tracks the online/offline status of ServiceNow users. It stores information about a user's availability, such as whether they are currently active, away, or offline. This data is used to indicate a user's presence throughout the platform. v_user_session Table provides a view of active user sessions within ServiceNow. It contains information about each user's login session, including the user, timestamp, IP address, and other relevant session details. sys_ui_list Table defines the layout and configuration of list views throughout the ServiceNow user interface. It stores the structure and customizations for how records are displayed in lists, including columns, sorting, and filtering options. sys_tiny_url Table manages shortened URL links within the ServiceNow platform. It stores the mapping between a concise URL and the full, original URL. This is used to create easily shareable links to specific pages or records in ServiceNow. isc_login_event Table records login events for users in ServiceNow. It stores information such as login time, user, IP address, and authentication details, helping to track and audit login activity. sys_ui_recent_selection Table stores the most recent selections made by users in the ServiceNow interface, allowing the platform to provide quick access to frequently used items. sys_hub_step_instance Table tracks execution instances of Flow Designer or IntegrationHub steps. It logs information about each step's state, execution time, and results for monitoring and troubleshooting flows. wf_activity Table defines individual activities within a workflow in ServiceNow. Each record represents a specific action or task, including conditions and transitions to other activities. wf_workflow_version Table stores version information of workflows in ServiceNow. Each record represents a saved version of a workflow definition, allowing tracking and rollback of workflow changes. wf_workflow_instance Table contains instances of workflow executions. It tracks the current state, start and end times, and overall progress of workflow executions for specific records. sys_journal_field Table stores journal entries such as comments and work notes added to records in ServiceNow. It enables tracking of communication and updates over a record's lifecycle. sys_audit Table logs field-level changes to records in ServiceNow. Each entry captures old and new values, user making the change, and timestamp, providing an audit history for data integrity. sys_history_set Table maintains sets of historical changes grouped together for a record. It helps organize and track changes as part of the system's auditing functionality. sys_ui_navigator_history Table stores navigation history for users in the ServiceNow UI. It keeps track of previously visited modules and pages for quick navigation. syslog Table stores system logs that capture events and messages generated by the ServiceNow platform. It includes information useful for debugging, performance monitoring, and system analysis. syslog_transaction Table logs transactional data for system operations in ServiceNow. It records transaction details, including performance metrics and processing information, to aid in diagnostics and optimization. sys_user_login_history TODO: Yet to Add description here. sn_instance_clone_request TODO: Yet to Add description here. discovery_probes TODO: Yet to Add description here. user_multifactor_auth TODO: Yet to Add description here.

Managing MID Servers often involves troubleshooting connectivity issues, dealing with locked user accounts, identifying the correct MID server dynamically, or executing commands directly on the host machine.
A common issue in ServiceNow is when a mid_server user role is assigned to a user that is not actively tied to a running MID Server, or vice versa, causing connectivity and authentication issues.
You might see alerts like: User snc_mid associated with down MID Server. No login attempts within reporting period. User mes_mid_ser with mid_server role not associated with a MID Server.

The following script dynamically identifies MID servers that are not in the "Up" state, removes their bindings, and cleans up the mid_server roles for users that shouldn't have them anymore. APIs Used: GlideRecord('ecc_agent_config') - Manages MID server configurations. GlideRecord('sys_user_has_role') - Manages user roles. MIDUserConnectivity(0).checkConnectivity() - Native script include to validate connectivity. javascript (function() { // 1. Delete MID Server usernames from ecc_agent_config where the MID Server is not Up var grEAC = new GlideRecord('ecc_agent_config'); grEAC.addQuery('param_name', 'mid.instance.username'); grEAC.addQuery('ecc_agent.status', '!=', 'Up'); grEAC.query(); while (grEAC.next()) { grEAC.setWorkflow(false); // Do not trigger business rules grEAC.deleteRecord(); } // 2. Get all mid.instance.username values for MID Servers that ARE Up var all_mid_user = []; var getMidUser = new GlideRecord('ecc_agent_config'); getMidUser.addQuery('param_name', 'mid.instance.username'); getMidUser.addQuery('ecc_agent.status', 'Up'); getMidUser.query(); while (getMidUser.next()) { all_mid_user.push(getMidUser.getValue('value')); } // 3. Remove mid_server role from users who are not in the valid active list var grSUHR = new GlideRecord('sys_user_has_role'); grSUHR.addQuery('role.name', 'mid_server'); grSUHR.addQuery('user.user_name', 'NOT IN', all_mid_user.join(',')); grSUHR.query(); while (grSUHR.next()) { grSUHR.deleteRecord(); } // 4. Run Validation Job (checks connectivity over the last 4 hours) new MIDUserConnectivity(0).checkConnectivity(4 * (60 * 60 * 1000)); })();

When building custom orchestrations or integrations, you often need to find a MID server capable of reaching a specific IP/Hostname with a specific capability (e.g., PowerShell, SSH, REST). APIs Used: MIDServerFinder MIDServerSelector javascript // Option 1: Using MIDServerFinder var midServerFinder = new MIDServerFinder(); midServerFinder.setRangesByIPOrHostname('10.10.10.5'); // Target IP midServerFinder.setCapabilities(['PowerShell']); // Required capability var potentialServers = midServerFinder.getMIDServers() || gs.getProperty('mid.server.rba_default'); gs.info("Selected MID (Finder): " + potentialServers); // Option 2: Using MIDServerSelector var mss = new MIDServerSelector(); mss.setCapabilities(['PowerShell']); var potentialServers2 = mss.findAgent('10.10.10.5'); gs.info("Selected MID (Selector): " + potentialServers2);
documents.s: 2. Dynamically Finding the Correct MID Server

documents.t: Sometimes you need to run arbitrary PowerShell commands on the Windows host running the MID server for diagnostic purposes without creating a full Action or Workflow. APIs Used: SncProbe.get('Windows - Powershell') - Triggers a probe. GlideRecord('ecc_queue') - Used to read the response payload. XMLHelper - Parses the XML payload returned by the ECC Queue. javascript var probeName = 'Windows - Powershell'; var ip = '127.0.0.1'; // Target localhost of the MID Server var midServer = 'Service_Now_DEV_AD_Cluster1'; // The exact MID server name var psCommand = ` # Retrieve and display hostname Write-Output "Hostname: $env:COMPUTERNAME" # Retrieve and display the current user Write-Output "Current User: $env:USERNAME" `; var now = new GlideDateTime(); var probe = SncProbe.get(probeName); probe.setName(probeName); probe.setSource(ip); probe.addParameter("script.ps1", psCommand); probe.addParameter("skip_sensor", true); probe.create(midServer); // Poll ECC Queue for the response var i = 0; var maxChecks = 20; while (i <= maxChecks) { gs.sleep(1000); // Wait 1 second before polling var ecc = new GlideRecord('ecc_queue'); ecc.addQuery('queue', 'input'); ecc.addQuery('source', ip); ecc.addQuery('name', probeName); ecc.addQuery('sys_created_on', '>', now); ecc.orderByDesc('sys_created_on'); ecc.setLimit(1); ecc.query(); if (ecc.next() && ecc.state == 'ready') { var data = ecc.payload; try { var helper = new XMLHelper(data); var obj = helper.toObject(); var result = obj.result ? obj.result : null; if (result) { // Print out the payload gs.info(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)); } } catch (ex) { gs.error("Error converting XML: " + ex.message); } break; } i++; }
documents.s: 3. Executing PowerShell directly on a MID Server

documents.t: If you need to quickly clone an existing MID server to point to a different environment (e.g., from PROD to DEV) on the same host machine: Create a copy of the ecc_agent folder on the host machine. Rename the folder appropriately (e.g., agent_dev). Open config.xml and modify the <parameter name="url" value="..."/> to point to the new instance. Modify config/wrapper-override.conf, updating the wrapper.name and wrapper.displayname properties to ensure the Windows Service name is unique. Execute the start.bat file (or install the service) to bring the new MID Server online.
documents.s: 4. How to Copy a MID Server for a Different Instance

documents.t: ServiceNow provides powerful Out-Of-The-Box (OOTB) REST APIs that allow you to interact with the platform externally. This guide demonstrates how to use NodeJS to perform bulk updates and search codebase assets externally.

While you can run background scripts natively, sometimes you need to manipulate data from an external CI/CD pipeline or integration server. The script below uses the standard Table API to fetch and update records in bulk. APIs Used: GET /api/now/table/{table_name} - Fetches a list of sys_ids matching an encoded query. PATCH /api/now/table/{table_name}/{sys_id} - Updates individual records based on the fetched IDs. javascript import fetch from 'node-fetch'; // Requires node-fetch if Node < 18 const INSTANCE = 'your_instance'; const USERNAME = 'admin_user'; const PASSWORD = 'admin_password'; const TABLE = 'incident'; const ENCODED_QUERY = 'active=true^state=1'; // Example: Active New Incidents const LIMIT = 100; const authHeader = 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(`${USERNAME}:${PASSWORD}`).toString('base64'); // 1. Fetch sys_ids async function fetchSysIds() { const url = `https://${INSTANCE}.service-now.com/api/now/table/${TABLE}?sysparm_query=${ENCODED_QUERY}&sysparm_fields=sys_id&sysparm_limit=${LIMIT}`; const response = await fetch(url, { headers: { 'Authorization': authHeader, 'Accept': 'application/json' } }); if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`GET failed: ${response.statusText}`); const data = await response.json(); return data.result.map(record => record.sys_id); } // 2. Update each record async function updateRecords(sysIds) { for (const sysId of sysIds) { const url = `https://${INSTANCE}.service-now.com/api/now/table/${TABLE}/${sysId}`; const payload = { short_description: 'Updated via External NodeJS API', state: '2' // In Progress }; const response = await fetch(url, { method: 'PATCH', headers: { 'Authorization': authHeader, 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Accept': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(payload) }); if (response.ok) { console.log(`Updated ${sysId} successfully.`); } } } // Execute (async () => { try { const sysIds = await fetchSysIds(); console.log(`Found ${sysIds.length} records.`); await updateRecords(sysIds); } catch (error) { console.error('Error:', error.message); } })();

ServiceNow Studio has a feature called "Code Search" that allows developers to find keywords across Business Rules, Script Includes, Client Scripts, etc. You can hook into this directly via the sn_codesearch REST API. This is extremely useful for running automated security scans or finding hardcoded sys_ids from your local machine. APIs Used: GET /api/sn_codesearch/code_search/search?term={keyword} javascript import https from 'https'; const keyword = 'TODO'; // Search term const INSTANCE = 'your_instance'; const USERNAME = 'admin_user'; const PASSWORD = 'admin_password'; function codeSearch(keyword) { return new Promise((resolve, reject) => { const uri = `https://${INSTANCE}.service-now.com/api/sn_codesearch/code_search/search?term=${keyword}`; const options = { method: 'GET', headers: { 'Authorization': `Basic ${Buffer.from(`${USERNAME}:${PASSWORD}`).toString('base64')}`, 'Accept': 'application/json' } }; const req = https.request(uri, options, (res) => { let data = ''; res.on('data', (chunk) => { data += chunk; }); res.on('end', () => { try { const json = JSON.parse(data); if (json.result && json.result.length > 0) { // Filter out tables that returned 0 hits json.result = json.result.filter(item => item.hits.length > 0); resolve(json); } else { resolve(null); } } catch (e) { reject(e); } }); }); req.on('error', reject); req.end(); }); } (async () => { console.log(`Performing ServiceNow Code Search for Keyword: '${keyword}'...`); try { const result = await codeSearch(keyword); if (result) { console.log(`Found results in ${result.result.length} tables.`); console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)); } else { console.log(`No results found.`); } } catch (error) { console.error(`Error: ${error.message}`); } })();

ServiceNow provides both legacy Workflows and modern Flow Designer for automation. Managing these effectively sometimes requires scripting—whether you are digging through legacy workflow data to find specific values, reverting versions programmatically, or writing advanced scripted approvals in Flow Designer.

If you need to find where a specific keyword (like an old email address or a specific URL) is used across all published workflow activities, you can query the variable values linked to workflow activities. APIs Used: GlideRecord('sys_variable_value') - Where activity values are actually stored. GlideRecord('wf_activity') - To get the workflow version context. javascript var keyword = "some_search_term"; // Keyword to search for // Construct partial matching query var query = "valueLIKE" + keyword; var workflows = {}; var tbl = new GlideRecord("sys_variable_value"); try { tbl.addEncodedQuery(query); tbl.query(); while (tbl.next()) { var wftbl = new GlideRecord("wf_activity"); // Link the variable value to the activity via document_key wftbl.addQuery("sys_id", tbl.document_key); wftbl.addEncodedQuery("workflow_version.published=true"); wftbl.query(); if (wftbl.next()) { var workflowName = wftbl.workflow_version.name ? wftbl.workflow_version.name.toString() : "Unknown Workflow"; var activityName = wftbl.name ? wftbl.name.toString() : "Unknown Activity"; if (!workflows[workflowName]) workflows[workflowName] = []; workflows[workflowName].push(activityName); } } // Output results as JSON var result = { result: [] }; for (var workflow in workflows) { result.result.push({ wfname: workflow, activityname: workflows[workflow] }); } gs.info(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)); } catch (error) { gs.error("An error occurred during processing: " + error.message); }

documents.t: If a newly published workflow version is causing issues, you can programmatically unpublish it and republish an older version by updating the wf_workflow_version table. APIs Used: GlideRecord('wf_workflow_version') javascript // Step 1: Unpublish the current broken version var getWfBad = new GlideRecord('wf_workflow_version'); if(getWfBad.get('<current_version_sys_id>')) { getWfBad.published = false; getWfBad.update(); } // Step 2: Publish the old stable version var getWfGood = new GlideRecord('wf_workflow_version'); if(getWfGood.get('<old_version_sys_id>')) { getWfGood.published = true; getWfGood.update(); }

documents.t: While Flow Designer allows low-code approvals, you may encounter complex scenarios requiring script. The "Ask for Approval" action accepts a specific string syntax to build rules dynamically. [!NOTE] Consider scripting as a last resort. Check out the Flow Approval CoE before writing custom approval scripts.

The syntax is built by concatenating the following string elements: [Ruleset] + [Rule] + [Who] + [sys_id list] Rulesets: Approves Rejects ApprovesRejects Rules: Any (Anyone approves) All (All users approve) Res (All responded and anyone approves) % (% of users approve) # (Number of users approve) Who: U (Users) G (Groups)

Approval Scenario Script String Syntax Approved by any User ApprovesAnyU[user_sys_id,user_sys_id] Approved by 50% of Group Approves50%G[group_sys_id] Approved by 2 Users or by Group Approves2#U[user1_id,user2_id]G[group_sys_id] Rejected by all Users RejectsAllU[user_sys_id,user_sys_id] Approved or Rejected by any User ApprovesRejectsAnyU[user_sys_id] Approved by Group OR Rejected by any User ApprovesAnyG[group_sys_id]OrRejectsAnyU[user_sys_id] All responded and anyone approves in Group ApprovesResG[group_sys_id] Example usage in a Flow Action Script: javascript // Example: Dynamically require 1 person from a specific group to approve var groupSysId = fd_data.trigger.current.assignment_group.sys_id; return "ApprovesAnyG[" + groupSysId + "]";
